/-!
# Erdős Problem 869

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/869](https://www.erdosproblems.com/869)
- [ErNa88] Erdős, Paul and Nathanson, Melvyn B., *Partitions of bases into disjoint unions of
  bases*. J. Number Theory (1988), 1-9.
- [Er92c] Erdős, P., *Some of my forgotten problems in number theory*. Hardy-Ramanujan J. (1992),
  34-50.
- [La26] Larsen, D., *Three questions of Erdős–Nathanson on asymptotic bases of order 2*.
  [arXiv:2603.03472](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.03472) (2026).
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos869

/--
If $A_1, A_2$ are disjoint additive bases of order $2$ (i.e. $A_i + A_i$ contains all large
integers) then must $A = A_1 \cup A_2$ contain a minimal additive basis of order $2$ (one such that
deleting any element creates infinitely many $n \notin A + A$)?

A question of Erdős and Nathanson [ErNa88, Er92c]. The answer is no: Larsen [La26] constructed
disjoint bases $A_1, A_2$ of order $2$ such that $A_1 \cup A_2$ contains no minimal basis of
order $2$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at
  "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/8822f7ddef30fadbd92e1c6ab4ed897af356af5e/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos869.lean#L3490"]
theorem erdos_869 : answer(False) ↔
    ∀ (A₁ A₂ : Set ℕ), Disjoint A₁ A₂ →
      A₁.IsAsymptoticAddBasisOfOrder 2 → A₂.IsAsymptoticAddBasisOfOrder 2 →
      ∃ D ⊆ A₁ ∪ A₂, D.IsAsymptoticAddBasisOfOrder 2 ∧
        ∀ d ∈ D, ¬ (D \ {d}).IsAsymptoticAddBasisOfOrder 2 := by
  sorry

end Erdos869

reformulations.difference: Minimality is expressed using single-element deletions, whereas ErNa88 and Larsen's introduction define it by excluding every proper asymptotic subbasis.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The order-2 asymptotic-basis property is upward closed under inclusion. If B ⊂ D were a basis, choose d ∈ D \ B. Then B ⊆ D \ {d}, so that deletion would still be a basis. Conversely, D \ {d} is a proper subset whenever d ∈ D. This equivalence was proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean as minimal_deletions_iff_proper_subsets and minimal_deletions_iff_minimal. Er92c and the problem webpage already use the deletion formulation.

sources_consulted: Erdős and Nathanson, Partitions of bases into disjoint unions of bases, J. Number Theory 29 (1988), 1–9: definition on p. 5 and §3, Questions 3–4 on p. 8. https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1988-25.pdf; located using https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/Erdos.html

Erdős, Some of my forgotten problems in number theory, Hardy–Ramanujan Journal 15 (1992), 34–50, especially p. 44. https://hrj.episciences.org/125 and https://hrj.episciences.org/125/pdf (bibliographic record located through Crossref).

Larsen, Three Questions of Erdős–Nathanson on Asymptotic Bases of Order 2, arXiv:2603.03472v1: introduction, Theorem 1, and §2. https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.03472 and LaTeX source https://arxiv.org/e-print/2603.03472
review.notes: The sole theorem faithfully states the question and its negative answer. The webpage and Larsen's paper agree with `research solved` and `answer(False)`. Scratch checks also proved that the basis predicate means eventual representation by exactly two summands, its negation means infinitely many missing sums, and finite sets cannot satisfy it. A concrete disjoint pair of periodic bases verified that the hypotheses are satisfiable. The linked external theorem has the equivalent negated conclusion and matching definitions; its source and non-Mathlib dependency were inspected for placeholders/custom axioms, but the external project was not rebuilt. The target file matches the committed blob.
